A token is a chunk that becomes one number.","headline":{"text":"Token = one chunk, one number","semantic":"concept"},"tags":["plain Paris","spaced Paris","shouted PARIS"]},{"beatId":"b2","narration":"A tokenizer turns text into tokens. Characters keep the vocabulary — the fixed list of pieces — tiny, but paragraphs become thousands of steps. Whole words leave new names no entry, so subword pieces sit between.","headline":{"text":"Vocabulary = the fixed piece list","semantic":"concept"},"tags":["single characters","whole words","subword pieces"]},{"beatId":"b3","narration":"Learning starts from raw bytes: two hundred fifty-six values, so any text can be written. Then count neighbouring pairs, join the most frequent — 't' plus 'h' becomes 'th' — and repeat.","headline":{"text":"Learn merges from raw bytes","semantic":"concept"},"tags":["raw bytes","most frequent pair"],"source":"A field guide to subword merges"},{"beatId":"b4","narration":"Early merges join common pairs; late merges build whole words. Encoding replays them in that order: 'the' becomes one token, an unusual word stays in pieces.","headline":{"text":"Merge order decides the splits","semantic":"concept"},"tags":["merge order"]},{"beatId":"b5","narration":"To encode new text, pre-tokenization cuts it into chunks that merges never cross. A space sticks to the next word; capitals break the pattern. So plain Paris is one token, and PARIS needs three.","headline":{"text":"Pre-tokenization = cut before merging","semantic":"concept"},"tags":["chunk borders","capitals split"]},{"beatId":"b6","narration":"Corrowby bills every request in tokens, yet the team budgeted from word counts. English replies ran about one point three tokens per word. A language rare in training needed about three times as many.","headline":{"text":"Word counts miss real tokens","semantic":"problem"},"tags":["billed per token","rare language"],"statCards":[{"value":"about 1.3","label":"tokens per word","sourceRef":"num-4"}],"source":"Field notes: counting tokens before you pay for them"},{"beatId":"b7","narration":"So Corrowby counts tokens with the exact tokenizer of the model it calls, and writes budgets in tokens per language. That reply with Paris now fits.","headline":{"text":"Count with the model's tokenizer","semantic":"resolution"},"tags":["exact tokenizer","budgets in tokens"]}]}
